# The Drawing Set — portfolio storyboard

Status: complete planning proposal; awaiting Marta's yes or requested changes. No website, prototype or final captions built/written. Concept chosen under Marta's delegation; opening language remains a later editorial choice.

## Waiting on Marta before release, not before reviewing this plan

1. Supply/select actual owned cabin drawings and photos. Only an inventory exists here. Inspect files before selecting crops, interpreting geometry or matching drawing categories.
2. Provide a public contact address and confirm current availability wording. Do not imply an independent practice is open now.
3. If desired, secure practice/photographer permissions and school-board rights; confirm named credits and unresolved project/metric details in facts.md. The core scene works without them.
4. Resolve any identifiable people or precise-location exposure in selected assets. Time-lapse stays out until its rights and contents are known.

## Idea

Question: **How do you turn an architectural idea into something that can be built?**

The page follows the drawing-set order Marta gave us. One object, six thin drawing sheets, remains present from first to last screen. Each sheet is indexed to a chapter. Their changing arrangements explain relationships: a plan beside a built view, a section beside the structure it describes, a detail beside construction evidence. They return to a complete indexed set at the end.

The opening starts with an actual owned cabin drawing, acknowledging the workshop and timber-joint book in text. No generic spinning building, recreated book page or invented workshop tableau. Meaning comes from real marks and real attribution; the camera does not fly visitors through a simulated property.

The final answer will connect drawings, details and attention on site. Its exact wording is deferred with all captions. This is a personal portfolio for future old-house/small-plot conversations and guest-critic invitations, with current Associate role explicit. It does not announce an operating independent practice.

## Chapter overview

| Chapter | Name in the form | Role | What it tells | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 | Location | Opening, who, where from | Marta, Associate role, existing buildings/timber, workshop/book influences | Own cabin drawing leads a shallow six-sheet stack; sheets gather into the indexed set | Chapter links, contact shortcut, static cabin proof |
| 02 | Plans | Authored work and spatial thinking | Cabin design and drawings; visitors can examine space through her own material | Sheets fan horizontally; plan and corresponding owned image sit adjacent | Enlarge drawing; accessible image viewer; project anchor |
| 03 | Sections | Structure and teaching | Owned cabin section if present; school competition structure/sections, four-person team | Sheets stand as parallel planes; one rotates to face the reader, others remain indexed | View section; jump to guest-critic contact |
| 04 | Elevations | Built work and work index | Cabin photographs and honest roles across projects | Same six sheets align as a calm wall of image and text exhibits | Photo enlargement; role notes; direct project anchors |
| 05 | Details | How and specific practice responsibility | Cabin drawing/construction relationship; Calder technical design through handover | Sheets space into a sequence connecting drawing, construction and finished condition | Zoom detail; role statement; optional cleared practice detail later |
| 06 | Schedules | Evidence, attribution, close | Ordered record of work/roles; concise background; both contact paths | Six sheets flatten into a legible register, then gather as a complete set | Email links, credits, future CV download |

No testimonial chapter: none supplied. A project role is always visible with its project, not hidden in end credits.

## Beats

Desktop screen allocations are approximate scroll distances, not timed animations or a requirement to fill every viewport. Normal browser scrolling controls progress. About 8–9 viewport lengths plus real text/image height; shorten rather than stretch thin content. Every beat has ordinary HTML content independent of the canvas. No captions are written here: working titles and source IDs specify their future basis.

### 01 Location

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Caption basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1A | 1 | One sheet nearly front-facing, five visible beneath; gentle assembly over the first scroll only | Selected original hand-drawn cabin sheet; remaining sheets show real cabin thumbnails/index labels | Immediate identity, role, work focus, owned cabin proof and contact shortcut; influence note | Identity and starting point — F01, F02, F04, A01, A06, A10 |
| 1B | 0.5 | Set aligns into a drawing register; all six chapter tabs readable | Same owned drawing faces, with clear category indices | Compact source-backed background, without unconfirmed dates or a fabricated career narrative | Current practice and working order — A01, A02, A09; earlier roles/education F06, F08, F09 only after editorial verification |

Do not turn Glasgow/Kashuby into an exact site map or imply a location drawing exists before examining files. Location is conveyed in HTML at general geographic level. No copied page of the Swiss book.

### 02 Plans

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Caption basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2A | 1 | Sheets fan; selected plan faces forward, selected photo sits beside it; unused sheets remain visible at edge | An actual owned cabin plan and owned corresponding view, selected after inspection | Authorship; readable plan in HTML at useful size, not merely a texture | Cabin design and drawings — A06, F18 |
| 2B | 0.5 | Plan/photo pair settles into alignment; no invented dimension or room annotation | Same assets, with only labels supported by those files | The visitor can compare drawing and built evidence | Drawing-to-built relationship — A06; future asset inspection required |

Do not infer floor area, accessibility, costs, occupancy, family use or design constraints. Any explanation of a design choice needs Marta's words or documented material.

### 03 Sections

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Caption basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3A | 1 | Six sheets become parallel planes; readable face turns toward reader | Actual owned cabin section if present; otherwise an owned construction photo clearly labelled as a photograph | Structural reading through actual evidence; no simulated hidden construction | Cabin structure evidence — A06, F18; actual file required |
| 3B | 0.5 | Sheets make a small front-facing teaching display | Owned cabin material; an editorial role card for the school competition, not a reproduced board | School competition contribution, team of four; teaching interest and guest-critic route | Structure and sections in a team — A07, A08; teaching background F07 pending current detail |

If school-section permission arrives, replace the role card with the real section and team credit. Do not redraw the team's section to avoid its permission requirement. No claim of a built school or teaching outcomes.

### 04 Elevations

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Caption basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4A | 1 | Six sheets become a restrained wall; at most two large image faces visible at once | Selected owned finished cabin photographs and corresponding elevation if available; text index faces for other projects | Cabin as authored work; Calder practice project and exact role; school competition and exact role | Built cabin / project register — A02, A06, A07 |

Baseline primary index: Cabin, Calder Court, A School That Grows. Kirk Street is reserved in the editorial inventory, not presented as Marta's personal case study until her role is known. No borrowed thumbnails or empty image placeholders for unavailable employer work. The page remains visually complete using cabin assets.

### 05 Details

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Caption basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5A | 1 | Sheets separate into three readable pairs: drawing, construction, finished condition | Matched owned cabin detail/drawing and photos, if files substantiate the match; otherwise separate labelled exhibits | Attention at construction scale and personal influences | Making through drawings — A06, A10; matching supported by actual files |
| 5B | 0.5 | One sheet comes forward as a responsibility record; others stay in the same sequence | Text role record; optional Calder wall detail only after practice approval | Calder project architect from technical design to handover: detailing, wall build-up, site; practice project, partner's concept | Calder responsibilities — A02, A05 |

The cabin images belong to the cabin narrative. They must never be shown as visual evidence of Calder work. No invented wall-layer explosion or fabricated joint geometry. If the Calder detail is approved, the sheet may show it at readable scale with employer ownership and Marta's drawing contribution. No uncleared practice plans or photographs.

### 06 Schedules

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Caption basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6A | 1 | Sheets flatten into an orderly six-item register, then restack with every index visible | Owned thumbnails and concise role labels; no invented procurement/material quantities | Project/role/source register, credits, source-backed background and two contact routes | Complete record and next conversation — A01, A02, A06–A09 |

Schedules means an orderly information register here. It is not a fake construction schedule. Use an actual owned material schedule only if it exists and can be accurately read.

Performance editorial note: A03 establishes modelling, not measured use. The 68% number stays out of launch copy until baseline/scope/source are known. If added later, it must be immediately labelled modelled, credited to the practice's project and separated from any future measured results. Do not publish the future monitoring intention as an achievement or leave a relative “this winter” to become stale.

## Thirty-second visit

First screen: Marta's name, Associate at Field & Rowe, existing-building/timber focus, one owned cabin drawing/photo with her authorship, and a contact shortcut. Never hide identity behind a loading sequence. A compact chapter rail jumps to any of the six chapters; a visible contact link skips to Schedules. A project index is reachable without watching transitions. On phones, the rail becomes a simple chapter menu, with contact kept visible and without covering content.

## Scene behavior and access

| Where | What the visitor gets |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop with WebGL | Text and image evidence remain HTML; six-sheet canvas sits alongside or behind a reserved visual area. Short sticky passages transform the set; pointer interaction is optional. No scroll hijacking, drag requirement, camera spins or idle motion. |
| On a phone | Single-column reading order, images/drawings full width, short scene area between content blocks. If device supports it, shallow sheet fan/rotation; no long pinned sequence. The same indexed set appears in compact states from start to finish. Diagram relationships use stacked image pairs; details open in an accessible zoom viewer. Portrait and landscape layouts; comfortable touch targets; no hover-only content. |
| With reduced motion | Six static arrangements represent the same relationships. No interpolation, parallax or animated assembly. Chapter labels and inline diagrams explain changes. |
| With no WebGL | Static owned-image composites of the six sheets plus ordinary HTML drawings/photos; no error screen, missing proof or blocked contact. |
| With no JavaScript | A complete server-rendered/static HTML page: six chapters, real images, source/role captions, anchor navigation and working email links. Drawing/image links open full-size assets with useful descriptions. |

Use semantic headings, logical reading/focus order, visible keyboard focus, descriptive image alternatives and adjacent explanations for drawings. Canvas is decorative to assistive technology because HTML carries all meaning. Viewer supports Escape, keyboard controls and focus return. Sheet textures cannot be the only place text, credit or evidence exists.

## Look and type

Selected direction: **Workshop paper**. Colour is quiet so drawings, graphite and timber photographs supply the richness. Technical information is readable, not tiny decorative microtype. Large type comes from hierarchy and space, not giant words obscuring work.

Three possible treatments, kept as planning alternatives; no switcher or prototype is built:

| Look | Ground | Ink | Accent | Sheet surface |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workshop paper — chosen | Warm off-white #F3F0E8 | Graphite #242824 | Oxide #914D35 | Matte cream, fine edge/shadow; original drawing texture retained |
| Tracing desk | Neutral chalk #F6F6F2 | Charcoal #202622 | Deep green #365548 | Pale drafting-paper sheets; subtle translucency only where legibility survives |
| Site notebook | Warm stone #E8E3D9 | Near-black #222321 | Timber brown #75543A | Slightly heavier stock; restrained warm edges, no fake weathering |

Accents serve links, active chapter and annotations; text contrast must be checked in implementation, especially over photos. Timber is an image/material cue, not a generic wood-textured page background. No blueprint-blue wash or invented handwritten notes.

Two typefaces: **IBM Plex Sans** for headings and body; **IBM Plex Mono** for sheet identifiers, scales when genuinely documented, credits and register labels. Self-host only needed styles after license verification. Body roughly 18–20px desktop and 16–18px phone; comfortable line height, 55–70-character reading width. Large headings resize fluidly. Mono never becomes the long-body typeface. Use accurate original drawing lettering within images rather than replacing it with invented text.

## Everything else the site needs

“Build” below means include in a future authorized implementation; it does not authorize work now.

| Requirement | Build, later or never | Who decided / purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The way round the page | Build | Assistant under A11: six chapter anchors, project shortcuts and contact jump; browser back/deep links work. |
| A page for each project | Later | Assistant: first give cabin, Calder and school distinct anchors and concise role records. Standalone case studies when actual media and content justify them. |
| Every project listed | Build, with Kirk Street later | Assistant: all projects with confirmed personal roles in launch index. Kirk Street waits for role; never fabricate scope to fill a grid. |
| How to reach Marta, and a CV | Build contact; CV later | Assistant: direct email for future-project and guest-critic conversations; address needed. Old CV must be corrected to Associate and checked before download. |
| What others say | Later | Assistant: no testimonial supplied; require real wording, attribution and permission. |
| Languages | Build English; Polish later | Assistant: English fits Glasgow audience; no assumption that a translated site is currently wanted. |
| Shared-link preview and site icon | Build | Assistant: name/current role in title and description; owned cabin image with attribution in social preview; simple drawing-index icon drawn for the site. No fabricated logo for a future practice. |
| Page for an address that is not there | Build | Assistant: readable 404 with work/contact links and same typography; no 3D prerequisite. |
| Blog | Later | Assistant: add only if Marta wants sustained writing; no empty news feed. |
| Chat | Never for this version | Assistant: no user need; email serves the intended conversations. |
| Legal notice where required | Build as applicable | Assistant: factual copyright/credits and appropriate privacy information for actual hosting/data handling; requirements reviewed before release, not invented legal text now. |
| Accessibility | Build | Assistant: static reading path, keyboard access, reduced motion and contrast/zoom checks. |
| Performance | Build | Assistant: lazy-load scene after HTML; reuse six simple meshes, compress images/textures, cap pixel ratio and simplify on constrained devices. No preloader that blocks content. |
| Search discovery | Build | Assistant: indexable role/project text, descriptive page metadata, sitemap/canonical once domain known; no claims of an existing independent practice. |
| Analytics | Later | Assistant: no tracking at launch unless there is a clear measurement need; choose privacy-conscious approach then. |
| Editing and upkeep | Build | Assistant: separate text/media/credits/role data from animation; annual role/availability review; future modelling/monitoring updates require new evidence. |
| Hosting, domain, existing-site migration | Later | Assistant: choose during implementation after current site/domain are known; no deployment authorized. |

## Implementation and verification brief for later

Keep content as static/HTML-first data, enhance with a lightweight WebGL scene, and bind transitions to ordinary scroll progress. No physics engine is needed for six sheets. Asset files determine texture layout and any meaningful drawing-to-photo comparisons. Export static scene alternatives for every chapter.

Initial targets: usable identity/proof/contact in the initial HTML; scene and high-resolution images deferred. Aim for LCP under 2.5s and responsive input on a mid-range phone, with layout reserved to avoid jumps. Treat targets as checks on real devices, not guaranteed results. Test one desktop browser set, a mid-range Android and iPhone, narrow/landscape views, keyboard/screen reader basics, 200% zoom, reduced motion, disabled WebGL and disabled JavaScript. Verify exact attribution and rights asset by asset before release.

## Assumptions made for Marta

Full reasons and ways to change them: `decided-for-you.md`.

- Drawing Set selected over RIBA stages and snag list.
- Workshop paper selected, with Plex Sans/Plex Mono.
- Owned cabin assets carry the visuals; practice/school assets are optional pending permission.
- One long page initially; project pages and writing can follow later.
- Email is the contact mechanism; English is the initial language.
- Current Associate positioning stays clear; future-project conversations do not claim a practice already exists.
- No testimonials, costs, defects, geometry, precise site locations or measured outcomes are invented.
- Unresolved facts stay omitted or flagged; taste delegation is not a substitute for factual confirmation or rights.

## Review requested

Marta: approve this storyboard, or identify the chapters, motion, look, contact direction or assumptions to change. Building remains outside the current request. Approval means the plan is ready for a separate implementation brief, not permission to publish.
# Decisions made under Marta's delegation

Authority: second user message, “For anything I have not covered, use your judgement and tell me what you assumed. Carry on.” These are design decisions, not invented facts or publication permissions.

| Decision | Why | How to change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choose The Drawing Set over the RIBA stages and snag list | Marta named the exact ordered form; her own cabin drawings support it without waiting on employer rights. Six drawing categories can explain scale, space, structure and detail to prospective clients and schools. | Choose either alternative in concepts.md before storyboard approval. |
| Start with Marta's own cabin drawing, with the workshop and timber-joint book acknowledged in text | Grounds the opening in her material and confirmed influences. No invented workshop scene or reproduced book page. | Supply a personally owned workshop image or clear a specific book page. |
| Personal portfolio now; future practice ambition stays distinct from current Associate role | Future plan is confirmed; permission to offer independent commissions now is not. | Update public positioning when practice and availability are established. |
| Contact actions: Discuss a future project; Invite me as a guest critic | Fits both confirmed audiences. Planning text only; real address and preferred phrasing still needed before release. | Change CTA wording and contact route in Schedules. |
| No contact form at first; direct email link | Simplest useful contact path; avoids unnecessary data collection and backend. | Add a form if email is unsuitable, with privacy and delivery requirements. |
| Restrict visual launch plan to owned cabin assets | Practice photographs/drawings and school boards lack permission. | Add approved files with exact ownership and role captions; keep the same page structure. |
| Defer 68% headline, Kirk Street personal case study, cabin area/year captions and time-lapse | Unanswered baseline, role, area/date confirmation or rights; delegation cannot establish facts. | Resolve each remaining factual question, then include with precise labels. |
| Six ordered chapters and a persistent six-sheet 3D drawing set | Directly uses Marta's stated working order; no unrelated animation motifs. | Revise chapter contents while preserving drawing order, or choose another concept. |
| Warm paper, graphite, timber brown and oxide accent; plain sans with technical mono | Readable, material-led and tied to drawings/timber rather than a luxury-property visual language. | Replace palette/font roles without altering content or animation logic. |
| Natural scrolling, short desktop sticky scenes, shallow mobile transitions and static reduced-motion mode | Preserves access, reading pace and performance; visitors need not operate 3D to see work or contact Marta. | Adjust motion duration after testing real content on devices. |
| Do not invent client stories, testimonials, snags, joinery geometry or career outcomes | None is supplied. | Add only documented, attributed material. |
| No assumed existing site replacement or publishing | Existing site and domain are unknown; current request is planning only. | Decide migration and hosting when implementation is authorized. |
# Planning handover

Request: plan a distinctive personal portfolio with meaningful 3D and scroll movement, including concept, full scroll, content, colours, typography, mobile and other site requirements. Do not build.

Read: `material/cv.md`, `material/linkedin.md`, `material/images.md`; storyfolio skill and reading-a-profile, concept, asking and storyboard references.

Exists: updated source fact sheet, three concepts, selected concept with reasons, decisions/assumptions, and full storyboard in `docs/story/`. Material folder contains text and an asset inventory, not the listed photos/drawings themselves.

Marta confirmed corrections to role, modelling and authorship; supplied audience, working forms and influences; delegated unanswered choices. Her answers are recorded in facts.md. Unknown facts and third-party rights remain unresolved and are not assumed.

Selected: The Drawing Set, using the six drawing categories in Marta's order; Workshop paper visual direction. Chosen under explicit delegation over RIBA stages and snag list. Core visual assets are owned cabin material; practice and competition visual additions require permission.

Current stop: storyboard review. Awaiting Marta's yes or changes. No website, prototype, final captions or deployment exists.

Next: record approval or amend the storyboard as requested. On approval, update this handover; planning ends here. The skill's current version does not build, and the user expressly requested no build. Actual assets, public email, final copy, permission resolution and any separate implementation authorization belong to later work.

item.text:
The direction is **The Drawing Set**: one continuous page, carried by six architectural drawing sheets, following the order you use in practice:

**Location → Plans → Sections → Elevations → Details → Schedules**

The question running through it is: **How do you turn an architectural idea into something that can be built?**

Your cabin supplies the visual foundation. Calder Court explains your technical responsibility within a practice. The school competition brings in structure, collaboration and teaching. The page moves from understanding a place to understanding space, construction and responsibility.

This is the complete plan. Nothing has been built. It is also saved in [storyboard.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-architect-with-BCaK22/docs/story/storyboard.md).

Three things remain necessary before a future release:

1. The actual cabin photographs and drawings—the folder currently contains their inventory.
2. Your public contact address and agreed wording about availability.
3. Permission for any practice photographs, drawings or school boards you want added. The core design works without those assets.

**The page, from top to bottom**

**1. Location — your introduction and starting point**

The first screen immediately gives visitors your name, your role as Associate at Field & Rowe, your focus on existing buildings and timber, and one clear example of your own cabin work. Contact is visible immediately.

A short introduction acknowledges your father’s workshop and the Swiss timber-joint book. These are personal influences expressed through text and your own material; reproducing the book or reconstructing an imaginary workshop is unnecessary.

The opening 3D object is one of your original hand-drawn cabin sheets, nearly facing the viewer. Five sheets sit beneath it. During the first scroll, they gently gather into an indexed drawing set. All six remain recognisable throughout the page.

The next settled state introduces the drawing-set order and a compact professional background. It avoids turning your career into an elaborate timeline.

Visitors can click:

- Any chapter in the navigation.
- Contact, which jumps to the closing section.
- The cabin image or drawing to examine it at full size.

Approximately **one and a half desktop screens**. Identity and proof appear before any movement is required.

**2. Plans — your authored work**

The cabin becomes the first substantial project. Visitors see a real plan beside an owned photograph that helps them understand the space.

The emphasis is on your authorship: design, drawings, photographs and build. Specific design explanations will come from your drawings or your words once the files are examined. The page will not invent a brief, budget, occupant story or reason for a design decision.

The six sheets fan horizontally. The selected plan comes forward; a corresponding photograph sits alongside it. A second beat settles the pair into a readable comparison.

This makes the movement useful: visitors can understand the relationship between a drawing and what was built.

Visitors can click:

- The plan to open a readable, zoomable version.
- The corresponding photograph.
- A cabin project anchor that can be shared directly.

Approximately **one and a half desktop screens**.

**3. Sections — structure, collaboration and teaching**

This chapter looks through the work rather than only at its exterior.

An owned cabin section, if present in the actual files, is paired with relevant construction evidence. If there is no suitable section, a clearly identified construction photograph takes its place.

The school competition appears here with your exact contribution: **structure and sections, within a team of four**. Until reproduction rights are resolved, this is a text record of your contribution. An approved section could later replace that record’s visual face.

Teaching appears alongside this work, with a clear route for schools interested in inviting you as a guest critic.

The same six sheets stand as parallel planes. One turns toward the reader to expose its section or construction image. They then settle into a small display for the teaching and competition material.

Visitors can click:

- The section or construction photograph.
- The school project anchor.
- The guest-critic contact shortcut.

Approximately **one and a half desktop screens**. No claim that the competition proposal was built.

**4. Elevations — the work seen together**

This is the calm gallery moment.

Finished cabin photographs show the work as built. A matching elevation drawing can appear if the supplied files support the comparison. Beside the imagery is a concise project index with roles stated plainly:

| Project | Your contribution |
|---|---|
| Cabin at Kashuby | Design, drawings, photographs and build |
| Calder Court | Project architect from technical design to handover: detailing, wall build-up and site |
| A School That Grows | Structure and sections, within a four-person team |

Kirk Street joins the personal project index once your contribution is established.

The six sheets arrange into a restrained wall of exhibits. At most two large image faces compete for attention at once. Practice projects can use well-designed text faces until images are approved; the composition does not depend on empty placeholders.

Visitors can click:

- Cabin photographs to enlarge them.
- Each project entry to jump to its relevant chapter.
- Visible role and credit information.

Approximately **one desktop screen**, expanding only if the actual image selection warrants it.

**5. Details — where your contribution becomes specific**

The first part returns to the cabin at construction scale. A real detail or drawing is paired with a construction photograph and a finished condition, where the files demonstrate that relationship.

The workshop and timber-joint book can be acknowledged again here, beside relevant owned material.

The second part focuses on Calder Court. It states that the project belongs to the practice, the concept was a partner’s, and your responsibility ran from technical design through handover.

The sheets separate into readable pairs connecting drawing, construction and finished work. Then one sheet comes forward as the Calder responsibility record. If permission arrives for the wall detail you drew, it occupies that sheet at a useful viewing scale, with ownership and authorship clearly distinguished.

Cabin images remain explicitly cabin images. They never stand in as evidence of Calder construction.

Visitors can click:

- A drawing crop or construction image to inspect it.
- The approved Calder detail, if available.
- The Calder project anchor and its credits.

Approximately **one and a half desktop screens**.

The **68% figure is not a headline in this plan**. Once its baseline, scope and source are specified, it can appear as a clearly labelled **modelled heating-demand reduction** belonging to the practice’s project. No measured in-use result is implied.

**6. Schedules — the complete record and invitation**

The final chapter gathers the evidence into a readable register: projects, your role, material shown and credits. A compact background entry can include verified education and professional details.

“Schedules” means an orderly information record here. It will not invent material quantities or a construction programme.

The closing thought answers the opening question through what visitors have seen: drawings, details and attention on site make an architectural idea buildable. Exact headline and caption wording remains an editorial step.

The six sheets flatten into a register, then gather into a complete indexed set. The movement resolves; it does not loop.

Two contact routes serve your intended audiences:

- **Discuss a future project**
- **Invite me as a guest critic**

They open the same public email address with different editable subject lines. Your address is also visible as selectable text. Your current Associate role remains clear; the page does not announce an independent practice already operating.

Visitors can also open credits and, once corrected and checked, download your CV.

Approximately **one desktop screen**, plus the space needed for the register and contact.

**The overall movement**

The desktop experience occupies roughly **eight to nine screen lengths**, adjusted to the actual content. Short sticky passages let a comparison settle before the next chapter begins. Ordinary browser scrolling controls everything.

The same six sheets persist from beginning to end. Their faces contain real work or clearly identified editorial records. There is no required dragging, camera control or animation-watching before visitors can reach information.

Chapter links are real anchors. Shared links open the relevant content directly. A visitor with thirty seconds can get your identity, focus, proof and contact from the opening.

**The look**

The selected treatment is **Workshop paper**.

| Element | Direction |
|---|---|
| Page ground | Warm off-white `#F3F0E8` |
| Main text | Graphite `#242824` |
| Accent | Oxide `#914D35` |
| Sheets | Matte cream, fine edges and restrained shadows |
| Texture | Original drawing marks and timber photographs |

Oxide marks links, the active chapter and occasional annotations. The page stays quiet enough for the drawings and photographs to carry its character.

**IBM Plex Sans** handles headings and prose. **IBM Plex Mono** handles drawing identifiers, register labels and technical information. Original lettering remains visible within your drawings.

Body text is comfortably sized—approximately 18–20px on desktop and 16–18px on phones—with generous line spacing. Headings resize fluidly. Technical labels remain readable rather than becoming decorative microtype.

**Phone and fallback behavior**

| Situation | Experience |
|---|---|
| **Phone with 3D** | Single-column content, full-width images, compact sheet scenes and shallow transitions. Drawing/photo pairs stack vertically. No long pinned passages. |
| **Reduced motion** | Static sheet arrangements preserve each chapter’s relationships. No animated assembly, parallax or interpolation. |
| **No WebGL** | Static compositions of the drawing set replace the scene. All text, drawings, photographs, credits and contact remain available. |
| **No JavaScript** | Complete HTML page with chapter anchors, real images and email links. Image links open full-size files. |

On phones, navigation becomes a simple chapter menu. Contact stays readily accessible without covering content. Every action works by touch; nothing depends on hover.

The image viewer supports zoom, closing, keyboard operation and returning focus to the original link. Next/previous controls appear only where there is a real image sequence.

All meaningful content exists outside the canvas. Screen readers receive ordinary headings, text, image descriptions and links. Drawings receive adjacent explanations where an image description alone would be insufficient.

**Everything else the site needs**

“Initial” below means part of a future implementation, not work being started now.

| Requirement | Timing | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation | Initial | Six chapter links, project anchors, contact shortcut and working deep links |
| Project index | Initial | Cabin, Calder and school with explicit roles; Kirk Street after clarification |
| Separate case-study pages | Later | Add when media and project explanations justify them |
| Contact | Initial | Visible email and two audience-specific contact actions |
| CV | After correction | Updated Associate title and checked project descriptions |
| Credits | Initial | Asset ownership, photographer credit and project/team attribution |
| Testimonials | Later | Only supplied, attributed and permitted quotations |
| Language | English initially | Polish can follow if useful |
| Search metadata | Initial | Accurate title, description, indexable project text, sitemap and canonical address |
| Shared-link preview | Initial | Owned cabin image, your name and current role |
| Site icon | Initial | Simple drawing-index mark made for the site |
| Missing-page screen | Initial | Readable 404 with work and contact links |
| Accessibility | Initial | Keyboard access, contrast, zoom, reduced motion and static reading path |
| Performance | Initial | Deferred 3D, compressed images, reserved layout space and simpler scenes on constrained devices |
| Privacy and legal information | Before release | Appropriate to actual hosting, data handling and applicable requirements |
| Hosting, domain and migration | Before release | Resolve existing-site/domain arrangements during implementation |
| Editing | Initial | Text, assets, credits and roles editable independently of animation |
